context.guidance: Serialise only the fields a response needs, using explicit allow-lists or response shapes rather than whole models or nested records. Remove Personal Data Elements the requester is not entitled to see, so each response stays within the Purpose for which the data was collected under §6(1). Apply the same field limits on every route that returns the same record, as Rule 6(1)(b) requires for access control.

value.fix: Don't send whole `memories` records. Map each record to a response shape that lists only the fields this route needs, and leave out fields like user IDs, email, location, device or IP data, internal flags, timestamps the client doesn't use, and populated relations. For example: `const toMemoryDTO = (m) => ({ id: m._id, title: m.title, description: m.description, imageUrl: m.imageUrl, createdAt: m.createdAt }); res.status(200).json({ status: 'success', data: memories.map(toMemoryDTO) });`. Also limit the fields at the query itself (for example, `.select('title description imageUrl createdAt')` and `.lean()`, and no `populate` of user documents) so other fields are never loaded. Make sure the query only returns memories the requester is allowed to see (for example, `{ owner: req.user.id }`). Put `toMemoryDTO` in a shared serializer and use it on every route that returns memory records (list, get-by-id, create and update responses) so the same field limits apply everywhere.
